clue.text: Work with an old hand?

parts.note: a piece of writing produced the old way, by hand rather than typed or printed, so 'hand' means handwriting, not a veteran

explanation.surface: A job alongside an experienced worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hand' suggests a veteran colleague; here 'hand' is handwriting, and the work is a document written by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A handwritten document, or an author's text before printing, is the traditional sense of this word.

clue.text: Love to be sheltered by tree, climbing in beauty spot

indicators.note: the love letter is covered over by the tree, so the tree goes round it
in a down entry climbing means the tree's name is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the elm is a tree
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A lover hides in a tree, climbing it in a pretty spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns ELM into MLE, and 'to be sheltered by' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty spot is a small dark mark on the skin, which is what a mole is.

clue.text: Type of clutch only recently produced

definitions.meaning: a clutch is a batch of eggs, and fresh ones are described this way
just laid by the hen, so freshly produced

explanation.definitionFit: Eggs that a hen has only just produced are described with this term, and a clutch is a set of eggs.

clue.text: Be ruthless in career as a driver?

definitions.meaning: to be prepared to do anything at all to get what you want
a driver careering along who never halts would literally never stop at anything

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be willing to do anything, however ruthless; read literally it describes a driver who never brakes.

clue.text: Cut most of grass; including some that's chewed up

indicators.note: the shortened grass holds the chewed stuff inside it
most of the word means its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: cud is the food a cow brings back up and chews again

explanation.surface: Mow most of the lawn, including some chewed-up patches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims REED to REE, 'up' turns CUD into DUC, and 'including' puts DUC inside REE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut something, such as a price or a number, is to make it smaller: a plain synonym.

clue.text: Old tax-collector one's seen in the bar

definitions.meaning: in the Roman empire and the Bible, a collector of public taxes
the landlord who runs a pub is found in its bar

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a Roman tax-farmer, as in the Bible, and a British pub landlord, who works in the bar.

clue.text: Almost reject incentive

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so its final letter is removed

parts.note: to spurn something is to reject it

explanation.surface: Turning down a reward almost happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter, N, from SPURN.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is something that urges you on, so it is a synonym of incentive.

clue.text: Show-off given top position — company about to be sunk

indicators.note: the two short pieces sink down into the top position, so they go inside it

parts.note: a peak is the highest point
c stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A braggart is promoted to the top just as the firm is about to go under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be sunk' puts CO and C inside PEAK.
explanation.definitionFit: The male peafowl fans its tail to display, so the bird's name is used for a vain person who shows off.

clue.text: But one could turn left at the corner of the square

definitions.text: But one could turn left at the corner of the square

parts.words: But one could turn left at the corner of the square
parts.note: a turn of ninety degrees, as made at each corner of a square, can be to the left as well as to the right, despite the name

explanation.surface: Directions at a town square: you could go left at the corner.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'But' plays on the name: the angle at a square's corner is named for the right, yet one can turn left through it too.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninety-degree angle at every corner of a square has this name, which sounds like it only goes one way.

clue.text: Peer, seeing the fat Owl wobbling in

indicators.note: the shaken-up letters go inside the word for fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat

indicators.note: the letters of the word wobble out of order and settle in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A nobleman looks at a fat owl tottering in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wobbling' turns OWL into WLO, and 'in' puts it inside LARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior judge made a life peer to sit in the House of Lords carried this title, so is a peer.

clue.text: Finally stars in this original, and great, production

definitions.text: Finally stars in this original, and great, production

parts.words: Finally stars in this original, and great, production
parts.note: the first and greatest event of all, the origin of the universe, after which stars at last appeared

explanation.surface: A great original show at last has stars in it.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a review of a theatre production; it is the creation of the universe, the first and greatest production, in which stars eventually formed.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmological theory names the explosive origin of the universe, which eventually produced the stars.

clue.text: Stopped getting stuck

definitions.meaning: grinding to a stop, as gears or machinery seize up

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means came to a complete stop, like machinery grinding until it seizes, so it covers both halting and sticking.

clue.text: Sort of charisma shown, about .. to pass round liqueur

indicators.note: a sort of the word means a variant of its letters, rearranged
about means turned around, so the word for shown is read backwards

parts.note: something on is being shown, as a play or programme

explanation.surface: Charisma is shown, about to be passed round with drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges CHARISMA, and 'about' turns ON into NO for the end. The two dots in the clue are a printing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sweet clear liqueur distilled from marasca cherries, so it is an example of a liqueur.

clue.text: Frequently sentimental when leaving, at first

indicators.note: the opening letter departs from the word for sentimental

parts.note: soft means sentimental or tender-hearted

explanation.surface: Often someone gets sentimental at the start of a farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving, at first' drops the first letter, S, from SOFT.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old poetic word for often, a direct synonym of frequently.

clue.text: Likely to be offered a clutch that's easily obtainable

definitions.text: Likely to be offered a clutch
definitions.meaning: available for anyone to grab or clutch at
free for anyone who wants to take it

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means available to anyone who wants it, literally there to be grabbed or clutched.

clue.text: Long to bypass editor, one of the old school?

indicators.note: the yearning word goes round the editor, passing about it

parts.note: to pant for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A traditionalist yearns to go over the editor's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bypass' puts PANT round ED. A pedant was once a schoolmaster, hence 'old school' with its question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler for rules was once also the word for a schoolmaster, so it fits a person of the old school.

clue.text: It's *a nuisance hosting new relations, round for the cup

indicators.note: the nuisance word holds the other pieces inside it, as a host holds guests

parts.note: a pain is an annoying person or thing

indicators.note: round means the word for relations is turned back to front

parts.note: kin are your relations

explanation.surface: Having the new in-laws round is a pain, so out come the cups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns KIN into NIK, and 'hosting' puts N and NIK inside PAIN. The asterisk in the clue is a printing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A small metal drinking cup or pan has this name, so it is a kind of cup.

clue.text: Being popular, before setting up big-time, is essential

indicators.note: the popular word is placed in front of the other piece

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: in a down entry setting up means the two pieces are lifted to read backwards together

parts.note: large means big

explanation.surface: Being popular before making it big is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting up' turns LARGE and T together into TEGRAL, which follows IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential to a whole is a necessary, built-in part of it, a synonym.

clue.text: It could sharpen artistic technique and style, possibly

parts.note: oils is a painter's medium and technique
tone can mean style or manner

explanation.surface: Art method and style might hone something.
explanation.definitionFit: A whetstone used with oil for honing blades has this name, so it could sharpen a tool.

clue.text: Supply article with flower specified for border

indicators.note: the flower's name forms a border around the article

parts.note: the lily is a flower
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A supplier provides an article with a specified flower for the garden border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is not the verb to provide; it is the adverb of supple. 'for border' puts LILY round THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Supply here is the adverb from supple, meaning in a flexible, lissom way, a synonym.

clue.text: Take turns on a casual basis

definitions.text: Take turns on a casual basis

parts.words: Take turns on a casual basis
parts.note: to go for a turn, a short walk, in a leisurely relaxed way, not to alternate with others

explanation.surface: Share duties informally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take turns' suggests alternating; a turn is also a short walk, taken casually.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely walk, or to go for one, is a casual turn about the place.

clue.text: Act as tutor of poetry in Old English

indicators.note: the poetry word goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A teacher tutors in Old English poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts VERSE inside OE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor supervises a student's work, so acting as one is to supervise, a synonym.

clue.text: Set to acquire first of wisdom, and mature

indicators.note: the set takes in a letter, so it goes inside

parts.note: a set of things is a group

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Getting a little wisdom and maturing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of' gives W, and 'to acquire' puts it inside GROUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To mature is to become an adult, to stop being childish, which is this phrasal verb.

clue.text: About to pull inside, perhaps

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to tug is to pull

explanation.surface: Someone is just about to pull something inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns TUG backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The bowel or belly is an example of the body's insides, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Cocktail perhaps served where polar expedition sets off?

definitions.text: Cocktail perhaps served where polar expedition sets off?

parts.words: Cocktail perhaps served where polar expedition sets off?
parts.note: a drink offered to get guests chatting at a party, and the ship that cuts a way through frozen sea for polar explorers

explanation.surface: Drinks are served at the start of an Arctic voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses play together: a cocktail handed round to relax strangers, and the ship that clears a channel through pack ice.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names something that eases first social contact, like a welcome drink, and a ship that breaks through frozen sea.

clue.text: A wee bit of a dust-up, possibly cut short

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards
the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a mote is a speck of dust

explanation.surface: A small part of a scuffle, perhaps trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' trims MOTE to MOT, 'up' turns it into TOM, and A goes in front. 'possibly' marks the punning reading of 'dust-up'.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest unit of a chemical element is a tiny particle, so it means a wee bit.

clue.text: Vindicate using extremes, consumed by wrath? I might

definitions.text: Vindicate using extremes, consumed by wrath? I might

indicators.note: the end letters are swallowed up inside the word for wrath

parts.note: anger is wrath

indicators.note: the outermost letters, first and last, of the word

explanation.surface: An angry person asks whether they might be justified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes' gives V and E, the first and last letters of 'Vindicate', and 'consumed by' puts them inside ANGER. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: One who takes revenge in fury is acting to vindicate a wrong, which is what the clue describes.

clue.text: Interrupting humorist, possibly caps something indefinable

indicators.note: the caps break into the middle of the word for the humorist

parts.note: a wit is a clever, funny person, one kind of humorist
caps are hats

explanation.surface: Someone interrupts a comedian whose headgear is somehow odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Interrupting' puts HATS inside WIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial word for a thing whose name escapes you, so for something indefinable.

clue.text: Reported jams in flow of underground

indicators.note: reported means said out loud, so a word that sounds like it

parts.note: to jam is to stick, so jams means sticks

explanation.surface: News of a jam on the Underground railway.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the Styx is the river of the underworld; 'Reported' says that STICKS sounds like it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Styx is the river of the Greek underworld, so a flow of the underground world.

clue.text: Closely follow mistakes made by crew, crossing river

parts.note: slips are mistakes

indicators.note: the crew goes across, around, the river letter

parts.note: a crew is a team

explanation.surface: A rowing crew makes errors while crossing a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts R inside TEAM, after SLIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride in the slipstream of another vehicle is to follow it closely, so the noun is used as a verb here.
